SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LANGUAGE STRUCTURES SCHOOL
Subject: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Language structures School helps you succeed in ENGLISH ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LANGUAGE STRUCTURES SCHOOL
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Appreciate the use of to her) object pronouns for 

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the use of to her) object pronouns for . You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the use of to her) object pronouns for .
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Language structures School”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the use of to her) object pronouns for . Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Recognise correct to have use of the forms of 

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise correct to have use of the forms of . You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise correct to have use of the forms of .
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Language structures School to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise correct to have use of the forms of . Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use present continuous  In small groups, learners take part in

What this means
In this part you learn to use present continuous  In small groups, learners take part in. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use present continuous  In small groups, learners take part in.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use present continuous  In small groups, learners take part in. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Language structures School is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Language structures School”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the use of to her) object pronouns for )

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Language structures School to a partner. (skill: recognise correct to have use of the forms of )

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: use present continuous  In small groups, learners take part in)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Language structures School to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate the use of to her) object pronouns for .
3. Practise this skill: recognise correct to have use of the forms of .
4. Practise this skill: use present continuous  In small groups, learners take part in.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Language structures School from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Language structures School: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Language structures School?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

1. Know what Language structures School means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate the use of to her) object pronouns for .
